findings.item: 2. Guard test quality (real-config-driven, anti-vacuity, no tautology)
findings.citation: scripts/__tests__/camp01-live-browser-adversarial.test.ts:40-41 reads the REAL file: `const CONFIG_PATH = path.join(REPO_ROOT, 'playwright.config.ts'); ... readFileSync(CONFIG_PATH, 'utf-8')` -- not a hardcoded key list. `declaredRelativePathKeys` (line 85) is a general regex (`/^ {2}([A-Za-z_$][\w$]*): (['"])(\.\.?\/[^'"]*)\2\s*,/gm`) over that text, so any future top-level relative-path-literal key (not just globalSetup) is picked up automatically. `isNeutralized` (line 107) is a general policy (undefined/null, or an absolute-path string, or a non-string value) rather than a value transcribed from the implementation -- not a snapshot test. Anti-vacuity: the first `it` (line 136) asserts `declaredRelativePathKeys(configSource).length` is nonzero against the REAL config, so a broken/always-empty parser cannot pass silently. The fourth `it` (line 159) constructs a stub base config with a novel key (`storageStateSeed`) the generator has never heard of and asserts the guard names exactly that key (`toEqual(['storageStateSeed'])`) -- this is a genuine red-turning row, not an implementation mirror, because the expected value is derived from the guard's own general rule applied to a fixture the implementation cannot have special-cased. No `.only`/`.skip` present in the file.
